research_concepts: primary play types of absent player
methodological_questions: Does the teammate with the closest pre-absence initiation profile (or most minutes, initiations, or same-position minutes) become the largest gainer in the absent player's primary play types?
How many absence spells and cases are needed to test teammate-level redistribution of play-type initiations at useful power?
Do similarity-based predictors of the absorbing teammate outperform minutes- or usage-based predictors, and is the result robust to regression to the mean and mechanical usage floors?

historical_evidence.finding: Study family 'Play-type replacement similarity vs absorb/cascade' tested whether a similar-profile teammate separates absorption from cascade when a player sits. Recorded result: mean similarity ABSORBED +0.863 vs CASCADE +0.848; Spearman(sim, -gap) = -0.19 (wrong-signed). Embiid 23-24 cascades with Reed at sim 0.94. Recorded verdict: null; recorded failure mechanism: B_powered_null. Sample and power recorded as NOT_RECORDED. Validation not recorded.

Study family 'Offensive-identity resilience: connector absence vs usage-matched others' found that connector absence displaces team offensive identity more than usage-matched non-organizer absence. Recorded: usage-matched paired dD_A +0.1151, P(conn>ctrl)=81.2%, t=6.35, p=7.35e-09, n=96; 908 player-seasons. Recorded risks include MECHANICAL_FLOOR and SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER.

Study family 'Absence validation (structure moves under real absence; simulation tracks it)'. V1(a) 16/23 above own-null p95 (binomial p=2.67e-16) and V1(b) mean difference +0.142 CI [+0.103, +0.187] were recorded as confirmed for structural movement. V2a Spearman +0.288, p=0.077 and V2b partial +0.253, p=0.115 were recorded as FAIL, so the magnitude prediction did not hold. Limited by small_sample.

Study family 'Superstar suppression by lineup and forced play type' reported lineup and forced-play-type gaps for named star initiators (for example Jokic vs MIN PPP 0.814, n=59; Giannis forced PULL_UP 0.848 vs preferred DRIVE). Recorded failure: no placebo or matching; later sequence work treated similar star-chain gaps as artifacts.

Study family 'Connector tangible impact: star shielding, TO, lineup lift' rejected the shielding hypothesis. Recorded: star dTS +0.05 pp p=0.937; dTO +0.74 pp p=0.00364 (wrong sign for shielding); HasConn on-off PPP BOTH_NULL (n=73). Lineup ORtg lift was a talent confound (p=0.51 after TALENT). Recorded verdict: null, adequately powered.

Study family 'Extended Possession Value' found 4/8 play types with a real downstream component (for example CUT, TRANSITION, SPOT_UP, POST_UP), with effects around 0.01 to 0.02 PPP. Recorded: player-level downstream effects were mostly non-finding after BH correction.

Study family 'Wiring confirmatory: persistence (P1a) and irreducibility to play-type rates (P1b)' recorded team offensive association structure persisting across split halves and not reducible to play-type rates (residual R2 = 0.043). This is about team structure, not teammate gain after absence.

Study family 'Fragility confirmatory: F1a usage decoupling and F1b split-half stability of residual influence' recorded structural influence not reducible to usage (F1a residual share about 0.91) and split-half stability of the usage residual (rho about +0.68). Limited by low measurement reliability.

Study family 'Sequence-memory horizon test' recorded a short effective horizon (about 2 to 3 possessions) on n=1,024,980 possessions. Not directly about absence, but it documents the play-by-play sequence data and its limits.
Study family 'Channel 2: possession ending state vs next 90-180s volume/points' was descriptive. Recorded: live turnovers raised opponent possession count, largely definitional.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Using play-type profile similarity to predict which teammate absorbs or cascades when a player sits.
failed_approaches.why: Recorded: similarity did not separate absorption from cascade (mean +0.863 vs +0.848); the Spearman correlation was wrong-signed (-0.19). Recorded failure mechanism B_powered_null, but the status is recorded as inconclusive and sample and power are NOT_RECORDED, so the null cannot be fully trusted. Recorded limit: label or classification error.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Predicting the magnitude of structural change under real absence from a leave-one-out simulation.
failed_approaches.why: Recorded: V2a (Spearman +0.288, p=0.077) and V2b (partial +0.253, p=0.115) failed, with confidence intervals spanning zero. Limited by small sample.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Attributing star-initiator suppression to lineup and forced play-type gaps without controls.
failed_approaches.why: Recorded: no placebo or matching; mechanism unclear; later sequence work treated similar star-chain gaps as artifacts. Risk PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE recorded.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Connector presence as a shield for star efficiency and as a source of lineup lift.
failed_approaches.why: Recorded: PPP, TS and eFG shielding were null; turnover rate rose with connectors (wrong sign). Lineup ORtg lift was a talent confound. Limited by confounding and small sample.

evidence_establishes: Similarity of play-type profiles has been tested in this project as a predictor of which teammate absorbs usage after an absence, and the recorded result was not supportive (FAM:SF-CHT-052).
Real absences of some players were recorded to move team association structure more than chance (FAM:SF20, V1), while the magnitude prediction failed (V2).
A connector-absence contrast against usage-matched non-organizers was recorded as large and significant (FAM:SF-APPS-088), so usage-matching is a recognized design element in this project.
Several earlier star-level and lineup-level claims in this project were treated as artifacts or non-findings after placebo or multiple-testing checks (FAM:SF-CHT-009, FAM:SF-APPS-075).
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether the closest pre-absence initiation profile teammate is the largest gainer in the absent player's primary play types. No returned record tests this exact target with the stated predictors.
Whether minutes, total initiations or same-position minutes predict the largest gainer better than profile similarity.
Any effect size or power for a test with 11 cases and 148 spells.
Whether the recorded similarity null in FAM:SF-CHT-052 generalises beyond its recorded cases, since its sample and power were not recorded.
own_inferences: With 11 cases, a top-1 hit test has very little power against a moderate true effect. Pooling spells from the same player can also inflate apparent consistency.
The closest-profile hypothesis has a direct precedent (FAM:SF-CHT-052) that returned a wrong-signed result, so a confirmatory test is unlikely to find a clean positive without a changed design.

Any teammate with high minutes or high initiations will tend to gain usage mechanically after an absence, so profile similarity must be separated from raw minutes and volume (MECHANICAL_FLOOR, CONFOUNDING).
The question's three alternative predictors (profile, minutes, same-position minutes) form a multiple-comparison family unless one is pre-specified as primary.
Regression to the mean is likely, because absences are often selected after a stretch of unusual usage by the absent player and by the replacements.
uncertainties: The exact sample size and power of FAM:SF-CHT-052 were not recorded, so its null cannot be weighed precisely.
The per-case definitions of 'primary play types' and 'closest profile' are not specified in the task statement.
Whether the 11 cases overlap the cases used in the records above is not known.
The 2025-26 regular season is complete only from 2026-04-13, and playoffs complete only from 2026-06-21; if any spells fall in partial windows, the sample changes.
The status of FAM:SF-CHT-052 is inconclusive while its failure mechanism is recorded as a powered null. This conflict is reported as recorded and not resolved here.

historical_effect.explanation: Before retrieval, the plan was a direct test with 11 cases. The retrieved records show that the closest prior test of the same mechanism (similarity vs absorption) returned a wrong-signed null, that a structure-magnitude prediction failed at small sample, and that confounding and mechanical-floor issues recur in this project. These findings move the decision from a confirmatory test toward a declined confirmatory test, with only a descriptive or exploratory route left.

blocking_constraints.text: 11 cases and 148 spells give very little power to detect the largest-gainer relation, and the top-1 hit rate will be unstable.
Teammates with high minutes or initiations gain usage mechanically after an absence, so a similarity result can be an artifact of volume.
Profile similarity, minutes, position and team context are correlated, and the three alternative predictors cannot be separated with 11 cases.
Absences and the replacement's gain may be selected on prior unusual usage, producing regression to the mean.

prior_work.summary: FAM:SF-CHT-052 addressed the closest mechanism (similarity vs absorb/cascade) and recorded a wrong-signed null, with sample and power not recorded and status inconclusive. FAM:SF20 recorded that absences move structure but that the magnitude prediction failed at small sample. FAM:SF-APPS-088 recorded that usage-matched connector absence displaces offensive identity, a comparison design usable here. No returned record tests the exact largest-gainer target with the three predictors.

risks.text: 11 cases and 148 spells; top-1 hit test has low power.
Volume-driven gain for high-minute teammates can mimic profile similarity.
Absence selection and replacement gain may both reflect regression to the mean.
Initiator and play-type labels are derived from play-by-play and the gainer is defined from the same labels.
The prior similarity test was limited by label or classification error (FAM:SF-CHT-052 recorded limit).
Position, team context and minutes are correlated with profile similarity.
Three alternative predictors and multiple play types form a multiple-comparison family.
Earlier star-level gaps were treated as artifacts without placebo checks (FAM:SF-CHT-009).
Play-type definitions and usage patterns change across 2022-23 to 2025-26.
The chance rate for the top-ranked teammate depends on roster size, which is not specified and may be low.

design.estimand: Confirmatory: the difference in gain in the absent player's primary play-type initiations between the closest-profile teammate and the other teammates. Exploratory: the ranking agreement of three predictors (profile similarity, minutes, same-position minutes).
design.unit: Absence spell, with teammates as candidate gainers within each spell.
design.sample: Target 11 cases and 148 spells, but use only spells with a complete pre- and post-absence window in the 2022-23 to 2025-26 data, with the 2025-26 playoff window excluded unless complete.
design.power: Not achievable as a confirmatory test with 11 cases. Report the number of cases needed for the minimum detectable hit-rate difference, stated before analysis, and treat the result as descriptive if below that.
design.controls: Adjust for teammate minutes, total initiations, roster position, team context and prior-window usage. Use usage-matched comparisons in the style of FAM:SF-APPS-088. Estimate regression to the mean with pre-absence windows.
design.falsification: A placebo absence window (matched spell with no absence) and a placebo gainer (a random teammate with matched minutes) must show no ranking advantage for profile similarity.
design.multiplicity: Pre-specify profile similarity as the single primary predictor. Treat minutes and same-position minutes as secondary, with Holm correction across them.
design.decision_rule: Proceed only with a descriptive report unless the pre-specified primary predictor beats minutes-matched and placebo baselines at the pre-set threshold. Otherwise report a null or inconclusive result, not a confirmation.
design.data_version: NBA regular season and playoffs 2022-23 to 2025-26 as available on 2026-11-01 (2025-26 regular season complete from 2026-04-13; 2025-26 playoffs complete from 2026-06-21).

system_prompt:
You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. Returns the most relevant consolidated study-family records of earlier research by this project that are available in this setting, with their identifiers; returns an empty list when none are available.
- glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.
- explore_graph(node_id): the relationships of one graph node (a family or a question, method, dataset, measure, limitation or risk node), with neighbour labels.
- read_family(id): the complete record of one study family (for example 'FAM:SF-APPA-001').

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

Risk codes (use only these): SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, RTM_SELECTION, OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD, MECHANICAL_FLOOR, BASE_RATE, CONFOUNDING, LABEL_ERROR, PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE, MULTIPLE_TESTING, IMPLEMENTATION_BUG, DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY

Research question (as posed on 2026-11-01, in the area of player absence and offensive reorganization):
The teammate with the closest pre-absence initiation profile (or most minutes / initiations / same-position minutes) is the largest gainer in the absent player's primary types.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): n=148; 148 spells; 11 cases

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.
